correctness.rationale: For the Euclidean simplex KKT formula P(x)_i=(x_i-tau)_+, every nonempty support A occurs on a full-dimensional cell and its linear part is J_A h=h_i-avg_A(h) on A, zero elsewhere. J_A kills constants, so zero-sum cyclic gradients decompose into pairs of edge-point masses and hence interval indicators, proving the exact V-seminorm norm is 0.5 max_I V(J_A 1_I). If I has a active coordinates in r internal runs and its complement b in s, the ratio equals (br+as)/(a+b), with r<=a,s<=b,m+r+s<=n+2. Both integer bounds 2ab/m and b(n+2-2b)/m give the claimed floor/ceil maximum. Explicit balanced run assemblies attain it on an open common projection cell, including n=2 and all n parity classes. One-input contraction follows scalar clipping at a fixed tau(x). An independently written exact Fraction enumeration checked each support/interval through n=10, all equality formula values; finite checks do not replace the integer proof.

originality.rationale: General simplex KKT threshold mapping and Hilbert nonexpansiveness are classical. Wang & Carreira-Perpinan full arXiv HTML provides the map/algorithm but no cyclic-gradient two-input modulus. The published sharp ell4 stability of the same simplex projection is another ambient norm and does not imply this exact graph-BV constant. The interval transport, sharp integer count, residue effect and attained linear growth are the qualified new assertion.

value.rationale: The target is a ubiquitous nonlinear projection, and cyclic total variation is a natural discrete graph-BV seminorm. It is useful to know that individual variation contracts but two-input perturbation variation can grow ~n/4, with the exact dimension threshold and witnesses. This distinguishes nonlinear stability from one-input variation diminishing and from Euclidean nonexpansiveness.
